propositions: Every command grammar must be built by a single side-effect-free stdlib argparse factory used by both runtime execution and build-time generation, eliminating manual syntax authority and hand-maintained help resources.

Runtime overview and help output must read from byte-current generated package-help artifacts before operation/config/mount/handler resolution, ensuring help is pre-operation and works on no-extras wheels.

A canonical lazy route registry must record command identity, spellings/visibility, handlers, parser factories, capabilities, and mount/init policy with exact aliases reusing canonical grammar/help and hidden commands explicitly helpable but undiscoverable.

Semantic capability registry must map capabilities to packaging extras and missing postures (error/unavailable/abstain/fallback) without eager optional imports, with checks deferred until selected mode/backend is known.

CLI reference generation, coverage checks, and wheel validation must enumerate registries and parser artifacts rather than source regexes or manual command censuses to eliminate duplicate authorities.

Lazy execution must preserve mount/init, argv handling, confirmation, stream, exit-code, and legacy-output contracts except for approved help normalization, with all 21 intercept-only commands given canonical help and safe dispatch metadata.
